A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToolEVO framework and ToolQA-D benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, API-perturbation studies, component ablations, and case/error analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Tables 2–5 and 7, the perturbation studies, and the Appendix C case analyses.

M1.justification: Cached-rollout MCTS, self-reflection, UpdateTool, and supervised fine-tuning on successful trajectories remain unchanged. The new Algorithm 1 documents the existing procedure rather than establishing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven ToolQA-D datasets, Easy/Hard tasks, and static, in-domain dynamic, and OOD dynamic API environments. The revised SciREX sample counts concern settings rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 retain the same proprietary models, Llama3/Qwen2 variants, and Static-SFT comparators. Ablation and error-analysis comparator membership also remains unchanged; newly cited works are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 6 changes SciREX training counts from 248/393 to 348/493 for Easy/Hard and removes development-set columns. Appendix A.6 also omits the development-based checkpoint-selection rule. Section 4 retains the earlier training totals and development counts, so these are reported setting changes without reliable evidence of an actual split change or rerun.

E4.justification: The API-name, parameter, and response-format perturbations, tool-update/self-reflection ablations, and Appendix C case studies and 50-error-sample analysis are retained. No additional robustness or diagnostic experiment is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The unchanged collection of multiple search trees is not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Performance values in Tables 2–5 and 7 and plotted results in Figures 2 and 4–6 are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains ToolEVO-Llama3-8B averages of 61.6/28.3 for Easy/Hard. No new experimental outcome is reported.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, PUCT equation, value updates, reflection formulation, and training objective are retained. The reward definition moves from v1 Appendix A.2 to v3 Section 2.2; Algorithm 1 adds procedural documentation, not a new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The claims about investigating tool variability, introducing ToolEVO and ToolQA-D, and improving adaptation remain unchanged. More explicit references to fine-tuning clarify the training process already described in v1.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.4 discusses using collected search trees for reward-model-based RLHF, extending v1's suggestion of preference learning. This is an unevaluated applicability discussion; interpretations of the reported results and error-analysis limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds MCTS pseudocode, an API-modification prompt in Appendix D.1, and explicit code/benchmark repository pointers. It also explicitly states that baselines share the tool-update module. These improve disclosure, while removal of the checkpoint-selection rule reduces reproducibility detail; most hyperparameters and hardware information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds XAgent, two Chen et al. mathematical-reasoning works, and Qu et al. works on self-driven tool learning and a tool-learning survey. These extend the citations without substantially changing the paper's positioning around dynamic API adaptation.

P1.justification: Environment-feedback details move into Section 2.2, while benchmark motivation and dataset statistics move into Appendix B.1. v3 adds appendix contents and algorithm/prompt subsections and clarifies fine-tuning terminology. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds an algorithm display, an API-modification prompt box, and appendix contents. Table 6 is relocated and loses its development columns; Table 2 gains a formatting explanation. Existing figures retain their content, with Figures 3 and 7 repositioned.

improvement.justification: The pseudocode, API-modification prompt, and explicit code/data pointers improve inspectability. However, v3 removes the checkpoint-selection rule and makes Table 6 inconsistent with Section 4's training/development description. With unchanged empirical evidence and unresolved split/selection reporting, the documentation gains and reproducibility losses do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
